name: What adds the most cost to a room addition?

mainEntity.name: What parts of a room addition add the most cost in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What parts of a room addition add the most cost in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most expensive parts of a room addition are usually the hidden ones. Foundation changes, structural reinforcement, utility relocation, and HVAC integration often cost more than visible finishes. If the project involves a bathroom, kitchen, or second story, plumbing and framing complexity can increase quickly. Tight access, slopes, and older homes can add labor time and equipment challenges. Finish level matters too, because custom cabinetry, high-end tile, specialty windows, and luxury fixtures can move a project far above the base estimate. Homeowners should ask for a detailed scope that separates structural work, mechanical systems, and finishes. That makes it easier to see where money is going and where savings are possible without harming the build quality. The best budget is one that accounts for both construction and the unknowns that appear after demolition begins.
acceptedAnswer.description: The biggest cost drivers are foundation work, structural changes, plumbing, electrical, HVAC modifications, roofing, and premium finishes. Costs also rise when access is tight, the site is sloped, or the design requires moving major systems or reinforcing the existing house.
